flex.intendedUse: latency-tolerant/non-urgent sequential workflows, background-style tasks, non-production evals/data enrichment
flex.clientTimeoutGuidance: official Flex documentation recommends long timeout windows, approximately 10 minutes or more where appropriate
flex.architecturalWrapperNote: Gemini Flex provider API is synchronous. If VELNAR places Flex behind an asynchronous queue/background worker, that is a VELNAR architectural wrapper, not a provider API property.

standard.intendedUse: general application workflows / most interactive day-to-day applications
standard.unsupportedClaimsRemoved: Removed unsupported claims of typical 2–5 second latency, guaranteed sub-15-second behavior, and official 10–30 second timeout recommendations.

priority.overflowBehavior: requests exceeding Priority dynamic limits may gracefully downgrade server-side to Standard processing rather than failing immediately
priority.clientMonitoringRequirement: clients should monitor provider-reported service tier / downgrade behavior

corrections.replacement: Removed unsupported timeout recommendation; official documentation does not prescribe 10-30s
Flex API is synchronous; VELNAR may wrap it asynchronously

corrections.originalClaim: Interactive replacement forfeits all Flex savings
corrections.replacement: Flex remains available for background/economy workloads

corrections.originalClaim: Unverified traffic volume and cost projections (e.g. fallback <1% volume, cost <0.5%)
corrections.replacement: Removed unsupported projections not grounded in canonical VELNAR traffic evidence

optionA.name: Keep Flex interactive and revise global timeout
optionA.conclusion: REJECTED. Accommodating Flex (official latency 1-15 minutes) in synchronous interactive fallback severely degrades UX, exposes users to sheddable queueing spikes, and unnecessarily weakens DeepSeek fail-closed interactive protection.

optionB.name: Remove Flex from interactive fallback only
optionB.conclusion: PARTIALLY_FEASIBLE_AS_INTERACTIVE_REMEDY. Solves the immediate interactive 15s SLO mismatch. Removing Flex from the interactive fallback lane does NOT forfeit Flex savings from VELNAR, as Flex remains available for background workloads. However, Option B alone does not specify the complete dual-lane architecture or background execution model.

optionC.name: Split interactive and background tiers
optionC.conclusion: STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED. Formally establishes dual-lane architecture with strict separation of SLOs, routing roles, and execution models.

interactiveLane.flexProhibition: Gemini Flex MUST NOT be treated as a transparent synchronous interactive fallback
interactiveLane.fallbackRequirement: Interactive fallback must be separately certified; Gemini Standard and Gemini Priority are benchmarking candidates, not automatic replacements

backgroundEconomyLane.architecturalWrapper: VELNAR should wrap Flex in an asynchronous queue / background worker for product architecture where appropriate
backgroundEconomyLane.timeoutSpecification: Provider-specific timeout / job deadline independently defined (e.g. 10-15 minutes) compatible with official 1-15 minute latency guidance; strictly never subject to 15s interactive SLO

futureCertificationRequirements.priorityCertificationPolicy: Because Priority may gracefully downgrade server-side to Standard during peak traffic, future certification must verify requested tier vs provider-reported actual tier, capture downgrade telemetry, evaluate price attribution, measure post-downgrade latency against interactive SLO, and forbid automatic provenance PASS without explicit downgrade policy validation.
